thread:
emma_ops: Dawn handoff — quick summary from last night (02:00-04:30 UTC).

emma_ops: Pager at 02:16 from incident-bot: /v1/embeddings 429 spike (region: eu-west). Alerts showed autoscaler oscillation + cache thrash. Customers affected intermittently (small fraction but high p95 for some orgs).

infra-bot: :rotating_light: Pager created by anomaly-detector at 2026-03-15T02:16:08Z — metric: embeddings.rate_limit_exceed_count (eu-west) > threshold.

sam_oncall: Oncall notes — I took the page. Primary (US-EAST) was me, secondary is kai_sre (EU). I immediately rerouted some traffic to the fallback embedding model (model-id: embed-lite-v2) to reduce pressure.

kai_sre: Confirming — I verified nodes in eu-west were thrashing between scale-up and scale-down (scale events every ~90s). Root cause looks like a bad histogram from a small customer sending bursts that the autoscaler interpreted as sustained load.

sam_oncall: Actions taken:
- disabled burst-scaling policy for autoscaler eu-west temporarily (`PATCH /autoscaler/eu-west` with body: `{"burst_window_secs":300}`)
- bumped reserved pool by +6 GPUs (dedicated) for 45 minutes
- applied route rule to send heavy customers to west fallback: `route.add("customer-group:heavy", "fallback-pool")`
- opened a customer DM for the top 3 affected orgs (leah_support handling comms)

leah_support: Sent initial outbound to customers at 02:45 UTC — short note explaining intermittent 429s and that we're operating mitigations. No one reported data loss, only degraded latency and occasional 429s.

mike_platform: Deployed a quick protective filter at the ingress side to smooth out bursty traffic using token-bucket rate limiter (config snippet):
```
ingress.rate_limiter {
  capacity: 2000
  refill_ms: 1000
}
```
Applied to eu-west customer-facing ingress at 03:05 UTC.

sam_oncall: By 03:20 autoscaler oscillation reduced, eviction_rate down to baseline. We started to migrate traffic back in controlled batches at ~03:40. Monitoring p95 and 429 counts.

kai_sre: Note: we saw an associated spike in prefix-cache misses that amplified token generation latency — likely because the fallback model's cache behavior diverged. Logged follow-up in infra ticket #PLAT-4321.

infra-bot: Added runbook link: /runbooks/embedding-autoscaler-thrash.md (please read before further autoscaler changes).

sam_oncall: Current status at handoff (06:12 UTC):
- Service: embeddings — GREEN (no active pages).
- Autoscaler: stable with burst-scaling disabled in eu-west (temp).
- Routing: ~15% traffic still on fallback pool (gradually draining).
- Customers: 3 orgs saw elevated 429s for ~15m each; all acknowledged and on support watchlist.

emma_ops: Coverage and rotation: primary = sam_oncall (US-EAST) until 10:00 UTC; secondary = kai_sre (EU) until 14:00 UTC. After 10:00, sam hands to kai in case of EU follow-ups. If both are unavailable, escalate to mike_platform.

sam_oncall: Open action items (short list):
1) Re-enable burst-scaling with conservative params once we have steady 30m of stable metrics (owner: sam_oncall).
2) Postmortem prep: collect metrics, autoscaler logs, ingress rate limiting traces (owner: kai_sre).
3) Customer follow-ups: closing loop with 3 orgs and update status page if needed (owner: leah_support).
4) Add tighter guard in autoscaler to ignore single-customer histograms for 10m windows (owner: mike_platform).

kai_sre: Runbook edits proposed: add a section for "temporary fallback routing" and checklist: verify fallback model cache, throttle upstream clients, monitor p99-latency, inform support. I'll make PR to runbook now.

leah_support: I'll keep the customers updated and share transcripts in the ticket. No escalations to legal/compliance.

emma_ops: Coverage gaps / notes:
- We had limited EU-wide secondary coverage between 02:00–03:00 because kai had a partial outage on laptop VPN; sam covered remotely but primary/secondary handoff wasn't ideal. Recommend clarifying VPN recovery steps in the handoff checklist.
- Add a short runbook note for oncall to check `autoscaler.events` for >3 scale cycles in 5m.

sam_oncall: If anyone needs to follow up: PLAT-4321 for logs, SUPPORT-981 for customer comms, and ops-runbook PR #58 for proposed changes.

mike_platform: Suggestion: schedule a brief postmortem sync at 14:30 UTC today (20-30m) to cover root cause and permanent mitigation plan.

emma_ops: Next steps before shift end:
- sam: keep fallback routing at <=20% and start slow drain once stable for 30m.
- kai: draft postmortem outline and attach autoscaler traces.
- leah: confirm customers are satisfied and mark support tickets with postmortem reference.

sam_oncall: Acknowledged. I'll log actions in the handoff doc and ping here if anything spikes.

emma_ops: Thanks team — handoff complete. :white_check_mark:
